title: Supported module sections and the localization triangle on a ringed space
statement:
Let $X$ be a topological space with a sheaf of commutative rings $\mathcal O_X$, let $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$, and let $Z\subseteq X$ be closed, with open complement $U$. Work with sheaves of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and their unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. For a module sheaf $N$, define $\Gamma_Z(X,N)=\ker(\Gamma(X,N)\to\Gamma(U,N|_U))$, as a $B$-module. Denote by $R\Gamma_Z(X,-)$ and $R\Gamma(X,-)$ the unbounded right derived functors of these module-valued functors; sections on $U$ are viewed as $B$-modules by restriction of scalars. For every unbounded cochain complex $F$, if $F\to J$ is a K-injective resolution with injective terms [def-pur-kinjective-complex, def-sp-injective-resolutions], then $J|_U$ is K-injective and the sequence of complexes
$$0\longrightarrow\Gamma_Z(X,J)\longrightarrow\Gamma(X,J)\longrightarrow\Gamma(U,J|_U)\longrightarrow0$$
is degreewise short exact. These three complexes compute the corresponding three derived functors, and their short-exact-sequence triangle gives a distinguished triangle
$$R\Gamma_Z(X,F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(X,F)\longrightarrow R\Gamma(U,F|_U)\longrightarrow R\Gamma_Z(X,F)[1].$$
The maps are the derived support inclusion and restriction, natural in $F$, and independent of the resolution under the derived-functor comparison maps. For $Z_1\subseteq Z_2$, the kernel inclusions, identity on $\Gamma(X,J)$, and restriction from $X\setminus Z_1$ to $X\setminus Z_2$ induce a morphism of these triangles. The support maps compose, and the map for $Z_1=Z_2$ is the identity. No boundedness, quasi-coherence, compactness, or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.
